title: Reentrancy
description: A smart contract vulnerability where an external malicious contract can call back into the vulnerable contract before the first invocation finishes, allowing it to bypass state checks (e.g. draining funds).

title: Integer Overflow and Underflow
description: An issue occurring when an arithmetic operation reaches the maximum or minimum size of the type. Prior to Solidity 0.8.0, this could cause values to wrap around, leading to unexpected behavior.

title: Delegatecall to Untrusted Callee
description: Calling a contract with delegatecall allows the target contract to execute its code within the context of the calling contract, which can modify state variables or self-destruct if the target is untrusted.

title: Unprotected SELFDESTRUCT Instruction
description: If a contract allows anyone to call a function containing selfdestruct, a malicious user can destroy the contract and drain its remaining ether.

title: Unprotected Ether Withdrawal
description: When a function allows withdrawing ether without proper access control (like an onlyOwner modifier), anyone can drain the contract.
